title: She replied "ok." with a period 😬 #shorts
description:
You send a long, funny message. She replies: "ok." With a period. Your whole evening is gone… but she's on a crowded bus, typing with one thumb, wondering if YOU are mad at HER. 😬

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk

title: People like you more than you think 💛 #shorts
description:
You walk away thinking you said something weird… while they're thinking "That was nice." In a 2018 study, strangers talked, and again and again people underestimated how much they were liked. It's called the liking gap. 💛

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk

#psychology #overthinking #shorts
tags: people like you more than you think

title: Why "ok." with a period feels rude 😶 #shorts
description:
In one small study, one-word text replies that ended with a period were rated as less sincere than the same word without one. Two letters and a dot… and your brain writes a whole story. 😶

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk

#psychology #overthinking #shorts

title: Your texts don't sound the way you think 🪙 #shorts
description:
A text has no face. No voice. No smile. In a well-known study, people were confident their emails would be read the way they meant them, but readers did barely better than a coin flip at telling sarcastic from serious. 🪙

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk

#psychology #overthinking #shorts

title: A late reply. A "seen". Your brain panics. #shorts
description:
A short reply. A late reply. A "seen" with no answer. Psychologists call it rejection sensitivity: when you expect rejection, you see it in moments that are simply unclear. Fear doesn't need evidence. It just needs a gap.

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk

#psychology #overthinking #shorts

title: Think someone is mad at you? Try this 🧠 #shorts
description:
Next time your brain says "They're mad at you": 1) notice the move (it's mind reading: guessing, not knowing), 2) think of three other reasons, 3) ask. Most of the time the answer is: "Of course. Why?" 🧠

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk

#psychology #overthinking #shorts

title: Why a 2-letter text feels like a threat ⚠️ #shorts
description:
Your whole evening is gone because of "ok." You're not broken. Your brain is running very old software that treats a two-letter text like a threat… and most of the time, the answer is "Of course. Why?" ⚠️

Watch the full video: https://youtu.be/1nVuUlwU6Vk
